title: Lock-Out / Tag-Out: Packaging Line Press
summary: Make a machine safe before anyone works on it.
story: A packaging press can start by accident, or release stored pressure, while someone has a hand inside. Lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) is the routine that prevents it: stop the machine, cut its energy supply, lock the switch so nobody can turn it back on, release any stored energy, and only then prove it is dead. Skipping or reordering a step is how people get hurt, which is why the order is enforced here.

glossary.def: Standard Operating Procedure: the approved written steps for a task. Everyone follows the same ones.
Locking an energy switch off and hanging a tag on it, so the machine cannot be restarted while someone is working on it.
The main switch that cuts a machine's power supply.
A valve that releases stored pressure (air or hydraulic) that would otherwise stay in the machine after power is off.
Any departure from the written procedure. In a regulated plant each one is recorded.
A tamper-evident record of who did what and when, so an inspector can verify the training happened.

steps.instruction: Notify affected staff: sign the line-down notice on the supervisor board.
steps.hazard: Colleagues may restart the line unaware.
steps.wrongHint: Notify staff first, before touching any machine control.
steps.label: Supervisor board

steps.instruction: Shut the machine down using the normal STOP button.
steps.hazard: Cutting power under load can damage the press.
steps.wrongHint: Use the normal stop button to shut down before isolating.
steps.label: STOP

steps.instruction: Isolate the energy source: switch the main isolator to OFF.
steps.wrongHint: Isolate the energy source once the machine has stopped.
steps.label: Main isolator

steps.instruction: Apply your personal padlock and tag to the isolator.
steps.hazard: Without a lock, anyone can re-energise the line.
steps.wrongHint: Lock and tag the isolator before releasing stored energy.
steps.label: Padlock + tag

steps.instruction: Release stored energy: open the pneumatic bleed valve.
steps.hazard: Stored air pressure can move the press unexpectedly.
steps.wrongHint: Release stored energy only after the lock is applied.
steps.label: Bleed valve

steps.instruction: Verify zero energy: press START and confirm nothing moves.
steps.hazard: Skipping verification is the most common LOTO failure.
steps.wrongHint: Verify zero energy last, by attempting a start.
steps.label: START

quiz.text: Who may remove a personal lock from an isolator?
options: Only the person who applied it
After lock and tag are applied
Not required if the machine is off

quiz.text: What proves the machine is safe to work on?
options: A start attempt shows no movement
A colleague says it is safe

quiz.text: A step was done out of order. What do you do?
options: Carry on and note it later
Stop, report, and restart the procedure
Ask a colleague to sign it off
